title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In July 1986 Grothendieck was working on 'ateliers' for a 'géométrie des formes' and a tame ('modérée') topology. An atelier is a set A of 'shapes' with three relations: an inclusion-type order ⊴, a 'well-inside' relation ≪, and a binary relation |∘|. Σ is the ordered set of 'sous-objets', obtained by a closure X ↦ X^0 = Sup^0 X. L is a distinguished class of 'lozal'/point-like objects. The previous page sets out the hierarchy: general, spatial, local, faithful, ponctual, ensemblist, tame ('modéré'), maquette, discrete.

This page has four parts.

(1) End of the previous paragraph, on tame spatial ateliers. Grothendieck proposes also requiring that Σ be 'modulaire', which he writes as the law A ∧ Sup_i B_i = Sup_i (A ∧ B_i), 'as in a Boolean algebra'. He guesses this might force the atelier to be faithful. A margin note says 'to check', possibly 'Noeth.'.

(2) A question about points. For x ∈ L, is x^0 a minimal element (an atom) of Σ* = Σ \ {0}? Equivalently, if X ∈ A and X^0 ⊂ x^0, must X = x? Contrapositively, X ≠ x should give Coimp^0 x ⊄ Coimp^0 X. That means some Z satisfies Z |∘| x and Z not-|∘| X.
- This reading is consistent only if |∘| means disjointness/incompatibility and Coimp^0 X is the set of elements incompatible with X.
- He then reduces to the case X = y ∈ L. The reduction uses spatiality: x^0 is the Sup of the y ∈ L with y^0 ⊂ x^0.
- So it suffices that for x ≠ y in L there is some Z disjoint from x but meeting y.
- He notes this is automatic when x and y are themselves disjoint: take Z = y. The only real difficulty is when x and y meet.
- In modern terms this is a T1/separativity-type axiom on the points. It is exactly the separativity condition of forcing posets, which makes points atoms of the lattice of ⊥⊥-closed sets.

(3) Dated 15.7. He asks whether to develop sub-objects of an atelier, or sheaves on ateliers, or to stay within spatial ateliers only. He answers 'J'en doute !'.

(4) A draft lattice diagram of atelier types: S, LS, M, SF, E, MP, EM, Mq, with the letter list DEQEFLMPS and Mq, Div, v, p. It is redrawn cleanly on the next page as the 'diagramme des principaux types d'ateliers'.

The right half of the sheet is reused scrap: printing instructions for Récoltes et Semailles, Fascicule 0.
- Job n°574, 300 copies, recto-verso.
- Contents: page de garde; Lettre L1–L43; Table des matières T1–T10, whose last three pages were printed with fascicule 4 at 500 copies; Introduction (i)–(xxiii).
- Addressed to 'Melle Lacan'.
- It also carries a scribbled identity S∧T = S∧C(1∧CT), with '1−CT' and a nested-interval sketch.
errors: Terminology: the displayed law A ∧ Sup_i B_i = Sup_i (A ∧ B_i) is infinite distributivity (the frame/locale law), not modularity. Modularity is: a ≤ c ⇒ a ∨ (b ∧ c) = (a ∨ b) ∧ c. For an ortholattice of polars these sit in a hierarchy (orthomodular < modular < distributive = Boolean). What he writes is the strongest, distributive/Boolean, condition.

The reduction from X ∈ A to X = y ∈ L tacitly uses spatiality (every element of Σ is the join of the points below it). That is legitimate only within spatial ateliers, which is the setting he announced on the previous page.

The scrap formula S∧T = S∧C(1∧CT) is a tautology if C is a Boolean complement (C C T = T). If C is only a pseudocomplement, then CCT ≥ T, so only S∧T ≤ S∧CCT holds in general. Equality would need T to be regular.

ideas.what: Space described by a set of 'shapes' with inclusion, well-inside (≪) and disjointness (|∘|) relations, with 'sous-objets' Σ obtained by closure: a point-free / region-based foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Mereotopology / contact (proximity) algebras; regular-open algebra of a poset with incompatibility
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitehead, de Laguna (1920s), Clarke (1981), Efremovich–Smirnov proximity (1950s), Dimov–Vakarelov contact algebras (2000s); Cohen/Scott/Solovay for regular-open completions
ideas.where_published: Ateliers unpublished; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only calls for tame topology without this formalism

ideas.what: Requiring Σ to satisfy A ∧ Sup B_i = Sup (A ∧ B_i), i.e. to be a frame / Boolean, and conjecturing that this forces faithfulness
ideas.modern_name: Frame distributive law; distributivity of the ortholattice of polars
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff, von Neumann (lattice theory); Ehresmann, Isbell (frames)

ideas.what: Condition for points x ∈ L to give atoms x^0 of Σ: for x ≠ y there is Z incompatible with x but compatible with y; the only issue arises when x and y meet
ideas.modern_name: Separativity (forcing posets) / T1-type separation for points as atoms

ideas.what: Hierarchy lattice of atelier types (spatial, local, faithful, ensemblist, tame, maquette, discrete, divisible)
ideas.modern_name: Taxonomy of axiomatic frameworks for tame/o-minimal-style geometry

ideas.what: Printing record of Récoltes et Semailles Fascicule 0 (300 copies; fascicule 4 at 500 copies; L1–L43, T1–T10, Introduction i–xxiii)

missed.claim: The atelier formalism (shapes with a disjointness relation |∘|, sub-objects as closures Sup^0, Coimp^0 = set of incompatible elements) closely parallels two things: the regular-open completion of a poset with incompatibility, and Boolean contact/proximity algebras in region-based (mereotopological) theories of space. His point-atom criterion is essentially the separativity axiom. Grothendieck's 1986 program for tame topology via such region calculi does not appear to be linked in the literature to mereotopology or to forcing completions.
missed.quote: i.e. ∃Z∈A avec Z|∘|x, Z \overline{|∘|}X ? ... Il n'y a pb que dans le cas x \overline{|∘|} y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Contact-algebra and region-connection-calculus results (representation theorems, points as ultrafilters/clans) could directly answer his questions on spatiality, atomicity of points and faithfulness. This would help any reconstruction of the atelier theory as a foundation for tame topology.

missed.claim: Open question whether points of a spatial atelier give atoms of Σ, and conjecture that distributivity of Σ implies faithfulness; both left unresolved ('À vérifier'), as is the choice between sub-objects, sheaves on ateliers, or spatial ateliers only.
missed.quote: Il est possible que cela impliquerait que l'atelier soit aussi fidèle
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are precise lattice-theoretic statements that could be settled once the definitions on the surrounding pages are fixed.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly lattice-theoretic housekeeping inside an unpublished axiomatics. The interest lies in the unrecognised parallel with mereotopology, contact algebras and forcing completions, plus a small R&S printing record on the verso. Nothing here is a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: The relation |∘| appears to denote disjointness/incompatibility (and the overlined version compatibility). Only this reading makes 'Il n'y a pb que dans le cas x \overline{|∘|} y' consistent.
'lorsque on se ramène' is likely 'lorsqu'on se ramène'.
In the lattice sketch, 'MP' is probably 'M' or 'P' (cf. next page: FL=P, M), and 'Mg' should be 'Mq' (maquettes).
The letter list 'DEQEFLMPS' probably reads 'D E G F L M P S' (the type letters of the next page's legend); 'Up' is likely 'v, p' (vide, ponctuels).
